note: Adapted from the original description in Haviland (1898) Observations on termites; with descriptions of new species (Journal of the Linnean Society of London, Zoology 26: 358–442), in English; published under the genus Termes (now placed in Bulbitermes), with the alate, soldier and worker all described. The nest is built on the stem of a shrub, 1—2 feet above the ground. The original’s nest, type specimen number, distribution and plate (Pl. 25) were not entered; the original records the head width as “*8 mm” and “*7 mm”, read here from the context as 0.8 mm and 0.7 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate body length 7 mm, head chestnut, thorax and legs Isabella colour (pale yellowish brown), abdomen smoky brown above and ochraceous brown below; head oval, eyes and ocelli large and close to each other, fontanelle elongate; antennae 15-segmented; anterior margin of pronotum nearly straight, anterolateral angles hardly deflexed, posterolateral margins nearly straight; posterior margin of mesonotum rather broadly concave, that of metanotum narrower; forewing buds distinctly larger than hind wing buds; wings 12 mm long, ochraceous brown, with a yellow stripe on the posterior margin of the subcosta, media nearer the submedia than the subcosta, very faint at the apex but reaching the wing tip, may fork at the apical quarter of the wing, submedia with 8 branches, reaching one ninth from the wing tip; hind legs extending beyond the end of the abdomen; abdominal papillae absent. Soldier body length 3 mm, head width 0.7 mm, fulvous, antennae 12-segmented (rarely 13); nasus conical, its anterior surface almost in the same plane as the front of the head, with a distinct elevation at the junction of head and nasus (clearest in frontal view); mandibles reduced; postmentum shorter than wide; pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior lobe short and raised. Worker body length 4 mm. Very close to T. sarawakensis, but the soldier is smaller, the antennae are 12-segmented and the base of the nasus is slightly swollen.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body length 7 mm. Head chestnut; thorax and legs Isabella colour; abdomen smoky brown above, ochraceous brown below. Head oval. Eyes and ocelli large, close to each other. Fontanelle elongate. Clypeus slightly convex. Antennae 15-segmented. Anterior margin of pronotum nearly straight, anterolateral angles hardly deflexed, posterolateral margins nearly straight. Posterior margin of mesonotum rather broadly concave; that of metanotum narrower. Forewing buds distinctly larger than hind wing buds. Wings 12 mm long, ochraceous brown; posterior margin of the subcosta with a yellow stripe; media nearer the submedia than the subcosta, very faint towards the apex but still reaching the wing tip, may fork at the apical quarter of the wing; submedia with 8 branches, very fine towards the apex, reaching one ninth from the wing tip. Hind legs extending beyond the end of the abdomen. Abdominal papillae absent. Sternite of abdominal segment 7 of the female less than half as long as wide, posterolateral margins rounded; abdomen with secondary sclerotized plates, with hairs and pale pigment spots.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 3 mm. Head width 0.7 mm, fulvous. Antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 2, shorter than segment 4 (rarely 13-segmented, segment 4 shorter than segment 3). Nasus conical, its anterior surface almost in the same plane as the front of the head; distinct elevation at the junction of head and nasus, clearest in frontal view. Mandibles reduced. Postmentum shorter than wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior lobe short and raised. Hind femur reaching abdominal segment 7. Abdomen oval, tergites arched, ochraceous brown. Abdominal papillae absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body length 4 mm. Head chestnut. Antennae 14-segmented. Abdomen oval, arched dorsally. Nest spherical, built on the stem of a shrub, 1—2 feet above the ground. Type locality: Malay Peninsula (Singapore), type specimen number 98.
